themes.name: Receipts vanish without signal
themes.insight: 5 of 8 participants lose receipts when upload fails in low-signal places, with no error and no retained photo, so they keep paper or double-capture.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Half the time the photo's not in the app anymore.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: they take a picture of the receipt in the app, it looks like it worked, and then the next day it's just not there.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: In the first month? I counted at least nine missing receipts from shoot days alone.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: I'll attach a receipt and it'll start sending and then the signal drops and — it doesn't seem to come back.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I'd guess a quarter of field receipts in October needed some kind of follow-up.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Now I just take a regular photo with my phone camera first, as a backup, and then I do the app one when I'm back in town.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: That's the month, honestly. People doing the new thing and the old thing at the same time.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: Things just quietly don't go through.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: So they take the photo, it sits there spinning, and they put the phone down and drive.

themes.name: Approval chain too rigid
themes.insight: 4 of 4 small-team admins and finance leads (Dana, Tomás, Jordan, Ravi) cannot model a one-approver flow, so people approve the same expense twice and spend stalls when the approver is away.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: A nine-dollar parking ticket goes through the exact same three steps as a two-thousand-dollar equipment rental.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: So the same person gets asked twice, or we had to invent a fake approver to fill the slot.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: So every expense comes to me, I approve it, and then it comes to me again as finance, and I approve it again. And I can't merge those.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: For a team our size, a strict chain just doesn't make sense.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: For a firm our size, the whole multi-level thing is overkill.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: A thirty-dollar order of clay sits there for nine days because she's at a conference and the app won't let anyone else step in.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: I made the principal both the manager and the department head for their people.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: So right now every purchase goes to Monique, then to me, then to me again as finance.

themes.name: Card limits are unreadable
themes.insight: 4 of 8 participants were declined at the point of purchase because the app shows one number (budget, monthly limit or balance without holds) that is not the real spendable amount.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: Declines? I'd say six or seven in three weeks.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: But the app shows the budget front and center, so that's the number everyone looks at.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: Budget said fine, card said no.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: And the screen only shows one number. So I'm looking at four hundred and he's standing at a pump in the middle of nowhere with a truck that's empty.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: I've kind of stopped trusting the number on the screen.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: And the app doesn't show holds. It just shows what's been charged. So I'm looking at nine hundred left and the card's saying no.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I'm a controller. Controls are my whole job. I didn't find it.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: So a foreman tries to buy a thousand-dollar pump at the supply house and it bounces.

themes.name: Accounting sync loses coding
themes.insight: 3 of 3 participants using Xero or QuickBooks (Dana, Grace, Jordan) see class, client or grant coding drop or misland in sync, forcing manual re-coding while the mapping screen looks correct.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: In October, about half came through with no class at all.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: In practice, the first month I had to redo, I want to say, a third of the coded lines.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: But the mapping screen says everything is mapped correctly. That's the confusing part. It looks right and the result is wrong.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: And there were duplicates too. Some expenses synced twice.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: When Ledgerly sends the expenses over, the grant doesn't come with it.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: She said it's actually more work than the paper forms, because at least the forms had the grant name written on them.

themes.name: Invites go to wrong people
themes.insight: 2 of 8 participants (Tomás, Jordan) lost one to two weeks because onboarding emails went to the account creator or a general inbox instead of the employees. Only two voices, so treat as an emerging pattern.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: Except it didn't send them to the people. It sent them to me.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: Yeah, I'd say we lost a week, easily.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: But three program coordinators never got their invites.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: It said done. It wasn't done. Nobody had anything.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: When I invited the staff, some of the invites went to our general info address instead of to the person.

themes.name: Mobile app excludes some users
themes.insight: 3 of 8 participants find the mobile app unusable (gloved field workers, confusing navigation, unlabeled camera button for a screen-reader user), and the accessibility report went unfixed for three weeks.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: They're not going to take the gloves off to tap a little plus sign in the corner.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: I got a nice reply saying they'd pass it on. That was three weeks ago.

quotes.speaker: Grace Whitfield
quotes.text: I tried. Honestly, it's unusable for me. I couldn't find anything I needed.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: And on the camera screen itself, the shutter doesn't say anything at all.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The app? For my guys it's unusable. I'm sorry, but it is.

quotes.speaker: Hannah Cho
quotes.text: It's frustrating because it's literally one label. It's the one button the whole app is built around and it's the one I can't use.

themes.name: What already works well
themes.insight: 6 of 8 participants name something worth keeping: the cards, spend reporting, identity-provider offboarding, and for desk-based users (Priya, Ravi) the phone app.

quotes.speaker: Priya Raman
quotes.text: Honestly, I love the app. I know that's probably not what you hear a lot, but for me it's been so much better.

quotes.speaker: Dana Okafor
quotes.text: The cards themselves. People like having their own card instead of borrowing mine.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: The app is the best part. Like, the phone app is genuinely slick.

quotes.speaker: Ravi Desai
quotes.text: Whoever designed the phone app, give them a raise.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Mbeki
quotes.text: I'd say the cards are great, the staff love not waiting for their money.

quotes.speaker: Marcus Lindqvist
quotes.text: The reporting on the website is nice. I can see spend by truck, which I've never been able to do.

quotes.speaker: Tomás Herrera
quotes.text: When I disable someone in our identity provider, their Ledgerly access goes too, and the card gets frozen.
